context:
Use the existing CLI: `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch
--scale 0.01 --phases power`. Use the checked-in result JSON as the baseline
and the existing `benchbox compare ... --fail-on-regression 10% --format json`
command as the authoritative regression check. Start with one current run and
a generous threshold; if GH runner variance still causes flakes, create a
follow-up to medianize current runs without replacing the comparison engine.

For baseline refresh, document the procedure: maintainer runs the workflow
manually with a `--update-baseline` flag, commits the new JSON.
description:
Quality plan Phase 2d. The audit observed: "BenchBox does not benchmark
itself." For a benchmarking framework, this is a notable gap. A small
per-PR smoke run on a single fast platform/benchmark combo gives early
warning of orchestration overhead regressions (result builder, dialect
translation, validation passes, lazy-loading machinery).

Scope: DuckDB local + TPC-H SF=0.01 + power phase only. Compare wall-clock
to a stored baseline from main. Fail the PR check if regression exceeds 10%
(configurable). Store the JSON result as an artifact for trend visibility.

Reuse the existing `benchbox compare ... --fail-on-regression ...` path for
the regression decision instead of inventing a second comparison engine.

preserves.behavior: Total CI time per PR increases by ≤2 minutes (DuckDB TPC-H SF=0.01 power runs in ~30 seconds on GH runners)
